Chapter One: Discovering the Source of Love Within
Sometimes, it just sneaks up on you. Maybe you’re sitting at your kitchen table, hands around a warm mug, and there’s this quiet ache you can’t quite name. On the outside, your life might look full—maybe even picture-perfect. But deep down, something feels missing. That’s often when the search for real meaning begins—a longing not for more stuff, but for a connection that’s genuine and lasting.
In these small, ordinary moments, the idea of divine love starts to take shape. It’s different from ordinary affection or happiness that comes and goes. Divine love isn’t about following rules or fitting into a certain tradition. Instead, it’s about sensing that, at the very heart of everything, there’s a wellspring of love just waiting to be discovered. For most of us, this realization doesn’t come with fireworks. It’s more like a gentle nudge—a quiet, persistent invitation to look within.
Think about someone who’s spent years chasing approval and achievements, always pushing for more, only to end up feeling drained and empty. No matter how much they succeed, that emptiness doesn’t go away. Then, in a rare moment of stillness, they let themselves just be—no judgment, no expectations. And in that silence, something shifts. They notice, maybe for the first time, that love isn’t something to earn or chase after. It’s already there, quietly pulsing right beneath the surface.
That’s really the heart of the journey in Ama Dios. This book offers an invitation—to see that divine love, whether you call it God, the universe, or simply the source, doesn’t come from outside. It begins within. And it isn’t just for a select few or the especially devout. This love is the birthright of every single person, no matter their background or beliefs. The first step? Just turn inward. Listen for that quiet voice that’s been with you all along.
As days go by, you might notice how even the smallest moments become chances to wake up. Picture a parent, overwhelmed by the chaos of family life, pausing to watch their child sleep. In that peaceful moment, they feel a love that’s both deeply personal and somehow universal. The boundaries between self and other, between giving and receiving, start to blur. The love they feel isn’t just for their child—it’s a glimpse of something much bigger.
Most of us don’t realize how often we look for love in the wrong places. We try to find it through relationships, achievements, or new things, but the satisfaction never lasts. Ama Dios gently points out that true fulfillment is already inside us, just waiting to be uncovered. There’s nothing you need to add. It’s more about peeling away the layers of fear, doubt, and self-criticism that keep you from seeing what’s always been there.
Of course, this isn’t always comfortable. Old wounds and habits bubble up, asking for attention and healing. But as you keep going, you start to see that every experience—whether joyful or painful—can open the door to deeper love. The invitation is simple: turn inward, listen closely, and trust that the source of love is already within your reach.
Over time, coming back to this inner wellspring of love becomes a way of life. It’s not about being perfect or living in constant bliss. There are still tough days—moments of frustration, sadness, and confusion. But underneath it all, there’s a growing sense of peace—a quiet confidence that love is the foundation of everything. And that’s really the beginning of awakening. It’s the very first step on the path to union with the divine.
